senses.definition: To ask someone to talk through what they have learned, informally and in conversation, rather than making a request with a defined deliverable. What you want is in their head, not in any document.
senses.caution: It sounds casual while asking for open-ended time, and the whole cost falls on them. Sent cold to someone senior with no boundary on it - no length, no topic, no reason it has to be them - it reads as entitled, and to some it reads as asking them to do your thinking. Put twenty minutes and a specific question around it and it becomes easy to say yes to. The register is informal: right in a message to a colleague, wrong in a first approach to an MD you have never met.
senses.example: You've done two of these migrations. Could I pick your brain for twenty minutes before we commit to a design?

cues.text: A colleague has already done two migrations like the one you are starting, and you want half an hour of informal conversation rather than a document from them.
You are messaging someone in another department whose experience you need, and you want a phrase that makes the request sound small and easy to accept.
A friend of a friend has renovated a flat like yours and you want an hour of their time and, more usefully, their mistakes.
Your cousin has just been through the visa process you are about to start, and you want to sit down with them and ask everything.

distractors: To ask a colleague to read your draft closely and mark up everything wrong with it before it goes anywhere.
To question someone closely enough that the gaps in their account start to show, usually with other people in the room watching the exchange.
To bring someone onto a piece of work for a fixed period because of what they specifically know, with a scope and an end date attached. The arrangement is a booking of their time, not a conversation.

To collect views from a scattered group one at a time and write them up as a single position that can be circulated. The work is in the consolidation, and it is the write-up rather than any of the individual conversations that people end up quoting back at you.

To ask for something that costs the other person almost nothing to give: an introduction, a name, a link to something they have already written. The ask is kept deliberately small so that saying yes is easier than explaining a refusal, and it usually arrives with an apology attached.
